assessment_summary: I reviewed the guide and installation summary, then independently inspected the environment and exercised the running software. The guide's local-dev flow was executed from /workspace; .env confirms the local-dev profile with BUILD_OR_PULL_IMAGES=build, so the 'build' vs pull distinction from the summary matches. Docker inspection showed all five documented services present and stable (0 restarts): frontend :3000, backend :8000, ipfs0 (healthy), cluster0, and Open WebUI :3333 (healthy). I confirmed real behavior rather than file existence: the Next.js frontend returns HTTP 200 and serves the TruSpace login UI; Open WebUI returns 200; the IPFS daemon responds to the API version call (v0.42.0) and the IPFS Cluster responds to /id and /allocations. On the backend I verified the Express API is live — the health route is auth-protected (401), CORS preflight succeeds (204), request validation rejects incomplete payloads (400), and a complete register-then-login cycle returned HTTP 200 with a user object. Most importantly, the decentralized/decentralized-collaboration path was demonstrated end-to-end: registration and login created volumes/db/truspace.db (90 KB) and pushed userdata.json to the IPFS Cluster, visible as recursive pins and a cluster allocation named users/<nodeId>/<uiid>/userdata.json, with backend logs showing successful outbound calls to cluster0:9094 and HTTP 200 responses. Persistent data resides under /workspace/volumes/. One apparent gap — no standalone ollama container — was investigated and is expected: docker-compose-ai.yml runs the WebUI image ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:0.10.2-ollama with Ollama bundled, and AI is enabled (DISABLE_ALL_AI_FUNCTIONALITY=false), so the documented default (with AI) is satisfied. Limitations: the interactive wizard was run via the underlying configure-env.sh rather than stdin prompts (as noted in the summary), which does not affect the resulting configuration; frontend routes like /en and /en/login return 404 but the app is accessed via / and /login, consistent with the documented http://localhost:3000 entry point. No missing artifacts, failures, or required repair were found.
